title: Attention kernel optimization profiling - FlashAttention / paged / fused (notes 2026-03)
content:
Context and goal:

This doc captures notes from the latest round of profiling experiments focused on attention kernel optimizations: FlashAttention variants, paged attention (chunked/paged KV cache), and fused ops (QKV + attention + projection kernels). Goal is pragmatic: identify the best combination of kernels and memory strategy for our serving runtime to maximize tokens/sec while keeping p95 latency and memory footprint within production SLOs for long-context workloads.

Summary of findings (top-line):
- FlashAttention (FA) variants consistently reduce memory bandwidth and increase throughput for long sequences; measured throughput improvements of ~20-35% on H100 for seq_len 2048 compared to baseline cuBLAS-based attention, with p95 latency improvements of 10-20% depending on batch size.
- Fused ops (combining projection + attention compute + output projection in a single kernel where possible) reduce kernel launch overhead and intermediate memory traffic; observed ~15-30% reduction in p50/p95 for short-seq workloads (seq_len <= 512).
- Paged attention (chunking the KV cache by pages/chunks to avoid holding full O(N^2) buffers) materially reduces GPU memory footprint (2x-3x for very long contexts) enabling larger batch sizes, but introduces extra copy and boundary-handling overhead that can add 5-12% latency per token for small seqs. For very long context (>4096) the memory savings often outweigh the overhead and throughput rises due to being able to increase batch size.
- Combining FA + fused ops + paged KV provides the best overall tradeoff for mixed workloads: FA reduces per-token memory traffic, fused kernels minimize kernel launches, and paged KV keeps peak resident memory manageable. Implementation complexity is non-trivial; careful integration and fallbacks are required.

Hardware & models tested:
- H100 (80GB), PCIe host in our dedicated cluster; baseline comparisons also run on A100 (40GB) for sanity checks.
- Models: LLaMA-2-13B-ish transformer (arch similar to 8-split Q/K/V) quantized to q4_0 for throughput runs; smaller GPT-like 2B model used for microbenchmarks where memory isn't the limiting factor.
- Framework: PyTorch with custom CUDA kernels; FlashAttention v2 rewrite (merged locally) and our paged-KV runtime branch.

Experiment methodology:
- Use synthetic input traces (uniform random token embeddings) and recorded production prompt traces (sampled from real traffic) to compare.
- Profilers: Nsight Systems + CUPTI timeline for kernel timings, nvprof for per-kernel metrics (when available), torch.autograd.profiler for CPU-side timings. Also use nvidia-smi and DCGM for memory and thermal checks.
- Metrics captured: tokens/sec (sustained over 60s windows), p50/p95/p99 latency per request, GPU memory resident, number of kernel launches per token, GB/s memory bandwidth (measured at roofline where possible).

Detailed observations:
1) FlashAttention behavior by sequence length:
- Short sequences (<= 128): FA gives modest gains or is near-par with our tuned cuBLAS matmul path. The dominant factor for short-seq is kernel launch overhead and host-to-device loop overhead.
- Medium sequences (256-1024): FA starts to show clear wins, reducing intermediate memory writes for softmax and reducing global memory traffic. Measured +15-25% tokens/sec on H100 at seq_len=512 with batch=8.
- Long sequences (>1024): FA wins strongly when the implementation avoids costly full-size buffers. At seq_len=2048 observed +25-35% tokens/sec and ~2x reduction in memory traffic for the attention step.

2) Fused ops impact:
- Implementing fused QKV projection + attention (single kernel) eliminated an entire roundtrip of intermediate writes for Q/K/V and reduced the number of kernels from 6->2 for the attention path. For low-latency workloads (seq<=512) this translated to ~20-30% lower p95 latencies.
- Fused ops require careful synchronization and different launch parameters per head/seq combination; there are corner cases where register pressure increases and causes spill to local memory. We observed regressions for head counts >= 32 on A100 with certain block sizes.

3) Paged KV tradeoffs:
- Design: KV cache split into fixed-size pages (e.g., 256 or 512 token pages). On generation we only keep active pages resident and stream older pages in/out as needed. This reduces peak GPU memory at the cost of page-copy overhead when crossing page boundaries.
- Effects: For extremely long contexts (>=8192 tokens) paged-KV allows 2-3x larger batch capacity compared to monolithic KV. Throughput improved when batch size increased to fill GPU compute, even after accounting for page-copy overhead.
- Overhead: For short bursts or frequent small generations paged-KV delivered small throughput regressions (5-12%) due to page management. Also complexity around consistent KV indices and multi-request interleaving needs robust locking or per-request segmentation.

Bottleneck analysis (where cycles are going):
- Memory bandwidth dominates for long seqs. FlashAttention reduces global memory writes significantly (softmax + temporary matrices) which is why it scales better.
- Kernel launch overhead is a first-order cost for short sequences. Fused kernels show the largest wins here.
- PCIe/host-device transfers show up only when we page in/out KV on demand; PCIe overhead can dominate if pages are frequent and sizes are small. Using pinned memory and overlap + async copies mitigates but not eliminates.
- Register and shared memory pressure in fused kernels can cause occupancy drops; need autotuning for block sizes per head size to avoid spills.

Representative numbers (H100, LLaMA-2-13B-q4, single GPU):
- Baseline (unfused, cuBLAS matmul attention): seq_len=512, batch=8 -> 420 tokens/sec, p95=72ms, GPU mem=32GB.
- FlashAttention only: seq_len=512, batch=8 -> 540 tokens/sec (+28%), p95=60ms (-17%), GPU mem=30GB.
- FlashAttention + fused projection: seq_len=512, batch=8 -> 620 tokens/sec (+48% vs baseline), p95=48ms.
- Paged KV enabled (page=512): seq_len=8192, batch=2 -> baseline OOM; with paged-KV -> 120 tokens/sec, GPU mem=28GB (vs estimated 70GB resident if unpaged), p95 ~420ms.

Implementation notes and risks:
- Merging FA and fused kernels into mainline: need to expose runtime flags and graceful fallbacks. Some production inputs (weird head counts, rotary embedding variants) currently hit unimplemented code paths in our local FA patch.
- Testing matrix explosion: head count, d_model, seq_len, batch size, device type (A100/H100) - need an automated CI harness that runs a reduced matrix nightly and flags regressions.
- Correctness: numeric differences introduced by fused kernels (different reduction orders) must be verified against reference implementation and evaluated on downstream tasks (e.g., eval prompts) to ensure no quality regressions.

Action items / next steps:
- Short term (1-2 weeks):
  - Add microbench harness in CI that runs small synthetic workloads across devices for a selected matrix (we can reuse the benchmark runner in tools/bench/).
  - Implement autotuner for fused kernels to pick block sizes/head-splitting to avoid register spill.
  - Add production trace run comparing FA+fused+paged to current default on sampled real traffic for 24h to measure end-to-end impact. (Owner: Ravi)
- Mid term (3-6 weeks):
  - Integrate paged-KV with per-request isolation (avoid cross-request page eviction bugs).
  - Add async prefetch heuristics for paged-KV to hide PCIe latency; evaluate pinned memory and GPUDirect RDMA where available.
  - Prepare rollout plan with canary on Dedicated clusters and metrics/alerts for error rates and latency regressions.
- Longer term:
  - Consider implementing hybrid attention that switches internal kernels based on seq_len at runtime (short path: fused kernels; medium/long: FA).
  - Evaluate memory-aware scheduling: prefer paged-KV on hosts with low free memory to maximize global throughput across tenants.

Open questions:
- What is the minimal set of model shapes we should autotune for to cover 95% of traffic?
- Should paged-KV be an opt-in feature per-customer initially (security/complexity concerns)?
- How do fused variants interact with future quantization/runtime (e.g., q4_0 vs q8_0 pipelines)?

Notes to self / TODOs in the codebase:
- perf/harness: add a flag --trace-file to replay sampled production traces to the profiler.
- kernels/fused: add fallback scalar path for unsupported head sizes.
- paged-kv: instrument page hit/miss counters and expose as metrics in the console.

References / links used in experiments:
- FA local branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/842
- Design doc: confluence:redwood/serving-runtime/attention-optimizations
- Related ticket: SERV-1123

Appendix: quick checklist before rolling to canary
- [ ] unit tests for fused kernel correctness across head sizes
- [ ] benchmark harness in CI passing on H100 + A100
- [ ] paged-KV metrics (page hits, evictions) added to telemetry
- [ ] runtime flags to force kernel selection per-route

End of notes.
